topic: Purpose of Basic Control Skills Test
question: What does the Basic Control Skills test primarily evaluate?
choice_a: Ability to read a road map
choice_b: Fuel efficiency techniques
choice_d: Basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position relative to other objects
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test has you demonstrate basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12, Introduction

question: According to the manual, for what will you receive points during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Horn usage frequency
choice_b: Changing direction to gain a better position, crossing/touching boundary lines or cones, and final position
choice_d: Speed of completion only
explanation: The manual states you will receive points for changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and for your final position.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12, Introduction

question: What must a driver do before exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Roll down all windows
choice_b: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit facing the vehicle with three points of contact
choice_d: Honk the horn three times
explanation: The manual requires setting the parking brake, placing the vehicle in neutral, and safely exiting/entering by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12, Introduction

question: What is a 'pull-up' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: A penalty for excessive speed
choice_b: Stopping without changing direction
choice_c: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_d: Any forward movement of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: On which two exercises are pull-ups scored?
choice_a: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_b: Exercise 1 and Exercise 4 only
choice_d: All four exercises
explanation: The manual states pull-ups are scored on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing).
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: Are applicants penalized for an initial pull-up?
choice_a: Yes, every pull-up counts as an error
choice_b: No, pull-ups are never scored
choice_d: No, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is a 'back-up' during the Basic Control Skills test, and on which exercise is it scored?
choice_a: Any reverse movement of the vehicle; scored on all exercises
choice_b: Pulling forward to correct position; scored on Exercise 2
choice_c: A required maneuver at the start of every exercise
choice_d: Backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment; scored on Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
explanation: The manual defines a back-up as backing up on a forward moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, scored on Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: How many free back-ups are allowed during Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking), and is exiting the vehicle permitted?
choice_a: There are no free back-ups, and exiting the vehicle is not permitted
choice_b: Unlimited free back-ups; exiting is permitted
choice_c: One free back-up; exiting is not permitted
choice_d: Two free back-ups; exiting is permitted once
explanation: The manual states there are NO free back-ups, and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during Exercise 3.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What is scored as an 'encroachment' during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Failing to sound the horn
choice_b: Taking longer than expected to complete an exercise
choice_d: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or qualifying high unique parts
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle, other than the mirrors or certain high unique vehicle parts.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What is scored as a 'look' during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Making eye contact with the examiner
choice_b: Checking mirrors while driving forward
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check the vehicle's position while backing
explanation: The manual defines a 'look' as exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: How many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) versus Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: One free look on Exercise 2; two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_b: Zero free looks on either exercise
choice_c: Two free looks on Exercise 2; one free look on Exercise 4
choice_d: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing, and two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What may result from opening the vehicle door while it is moving (not in neutral and park)?
choice_a: An automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_b: No consequence
choice_d: A one-point deduction
explanation: The manual states that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: On which exercises is 'final position' scored?
choice_a: Exercise 1 and Exercise 3
choice_b: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_d: All four exercises equally
explanation: The manual states final position is scored on Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: What may result from failing to follow the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise as directed?
choice_a: A brief pause in the test only
choice_b: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated
choice_c: A retry of just that exercise
choice_d: No effect on the overall score
explanation: The manual states failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.1, Scoring

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop), how many times may the applicant stop?
choice_a: Up to three times
choice_b: Up to two times
choice_d: Only once
explanation: The manual states you may stop only once during Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed during Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing)?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
choice_d: Two
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one (1) free pull-up during Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking), what must the driver keep between the cone and the line while tracking forward?
choice_a: The trailer axle
choice_b: The left-most front tire
choice_d: The right-most rear tire
explanation: The manual instructs steering left through the opening while keeping the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), within how many feet of the rear of the alley must the rear-most part of the vehicle stop?
choice_a: Three feet
choice_b: One foot
choice_d: Five feet
explanation: The manual requires bringing the rear-most part of the vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed, and how many times may the applicant exit the vehicle, during Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: Zero free pull-ups; no exits allowed
choice_b: Two free pull-ups; exit a maximum of two times
choice_c: Three free pull-ups; exit three times
choice_d: One free pull-up; exit once
explanation: The manual allows two (2) free pull-ups and permits exiting the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times during Exercise 4.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: During the on-road driving test, what must the applicant do at all times?
choice_a: Exceed the posted speed limit to keep up with traffic
choice_b: Wear a safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Avoid using turn signals to save time
choice_d: Use only the left lane
explanation: The manual requires wearing your safety belt and obeying all traffic signs, signals, and laws at all times during the test.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, when does 'unsafe coasting' occur while approaching a turn?
choice_a: When speed drops below 10 mph
choice_b: When the turn signal is not used
choice_d: When the vehicle is out of gear for longer than the length of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle, where should the driver stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Where they can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead
choice_b: At least one full block behind
choice_c: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Only when instructed by the examiner
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap).
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: What must a driver do when approaching an intersection with a stop sign or signal?
choice_a: Accelerate through if the light is yellow
choice_b: Slow down but continue rolling through if no traffic is visible
choice_c: Come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind the stop line, maintaining a safe gap
choice_d: Stop only if instructed by the examiner
explanation: The manual requires coming to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: What is a driver prohibited from doing while proceeding through an intersection?
choice_a: Decelerating
choice_b: Checking mirrors
choice_d: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
explanation: The manual states do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the test, where should the vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with traffic flow but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_b: At the posted speed limit regardless of traffic flow
choice_d: In the left-most lane at all times
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: What must a driver do before changing lanes during the on-road test?
choice_a: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
choice_b: Change lanes only at intersections
choice_c: Only use mirrors, not turn signals
choice_d: Change lanes immediately when directed, without checking traffic
explanation: The manual instructs making the necessary traffic checks first, then using proper signals and smoothly changing lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.4, Lane Changes

question: After stopping the vehicle to the side of the road during the Stop/Start maneuver, what must the driver activate?
choice_a: The rear fog lights
choice_b: The high-beam headlights
choice_d: The four-way emergency flashers
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, the driver must cancel the turn signal and activate the four-way emergency flashers.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, which turn signal should the driver activate before pulling back into traffic?
choice_a: The left turn signal
choice_b: No signal is required
choice_d: The right turn signal
explanation: The manual instructs turning off the four-way flashers and activating the left turn signal when resuming from the stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should a driver reduce speed?
choice_a: Only after exiting the curve
choice_b: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_d: Speed reduction is not necessary for curves
explanation: The manual instructs reducing speed before entering the curve so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.7, Curve

question: What is a driver prohibited from doing while any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Looking both directions for a train
choice_b: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Keeping hands on the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states drivers must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

topic: Railroad Crossing - Bus/Placarded Vehicle Stop Distance
question: For buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards, within what distance range must the vehicle stop from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing (unless exempt)?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Within 25 feet but not less than 10 feet
choice_c: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_d: Within 10 feet but not less than 5 feet
explanation: The manual states such vehicles must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: After going over a bridge, what might the examiner ask the applicant to identify?
choice_a: The bridge's construction date
choice_b: The name of the engineer who built it
choice_d: The posted weight limit
explanation: The manual states that after going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.9, Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: When stopping for a student discharge, how far away from the students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop, at minimum?
choice_a: At least 20 feet
choice_b: At least 5 feet
choice_d: At least 10 feet
explanation: The manual states the driver must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: What must a driver do if the vehicle is equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission?
choice_a: Pop the clutch on every shift
choice_b: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_d: Ride the clutch to control speed
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.11(a), Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What is a driver instructed to avoid regarding gear usage during the road test?
choice_a: Selecting a gear based on engine RPM
choice_b: Using the mirrors while shifting
choice_d: Shifting in turns and intersections
explanation: The manual instructs not to shift in turns and intersections, and to select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.12(b), Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: What is the proper braking technique described in the manual?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible in all situations
choice_b: Ride or pump the brake continuously
choice_c: Use the parking brake for all stops
choice_d: Brake smoothly using steady pressure, and do not ride or pump the brake
explanation: The manual instructs not to ride or pump the brake, and not to brake harshly -- brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.13(c), Brake Usage

question: In which lane should a driver finish a right turn on a multiple-lane road?
choice_a: The lane closest to oncoming traffic
choice_b: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: The lane directly to the left of center
choice_d: Any lane that is open
explanation: The manual states you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.14(d), Lane Usage

question: According to the manual, when should a driver's hands leave the steering wheel during the road test?
choice_a: When the road is straight
choice_b: Whenever using a mirror
choice_c: Never, except when shifting, after which hands should return to the wheel
choice_d: During highway driving only
explanation: The manual states to keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and to return both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.15, Steering

question: According to the manual, when should a driver check mirrors and traffic during the on-road test?
choice_a: Regularly, and before, during, and after an intersection
choice_b: Only when changing lanes
choice_c: Only when instructed by the examiner
choice_d: Only once, at the start of the test
explanation: The manual states to check traffic and mirrors regularly, and to check mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.16, Regular Traffic Checks

question: When should a driver cancel a turn signal, according to the manual?
choice_a: After driving one more mile
choice_b: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_d: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
explanation: The manual instructs canceling turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 13.1.17, Use of Turn Signals
